purpose: Let citizens choose how much of an approved property answer to view without silently changing the investigation question, legal scope, evidence standard or underlying answer.
core_principle: ONE APPROVED ANSWER → MULTIPLE SAFE VIEWS

view_definitions.DIRECT_ANSWER: Show only the material answer to the stated question plus essential limitation and next action.
view_definitions.RELEVANT_HISTORY: Show only historical events materially relevant to the stated question and answer.
view_definitions.EVIDENCE_AND_LAW: Show the supporting evidence, legal basis, dates/versions and material limitations.
view_definitions.FULL_CONTEXT: Show the approved broader property/legal-life context within the investigation scope.

scope_invariants: Time scope remains unchanged unless a separately authorised scope change occurs.
Legal regime and applicable legal version remain unchanged.
Publication and privacy rules remain unchanged.
Changing view mode does not create a new legal conclusion.
rules: View selection changes presentation depth, not the underlying answer.
Direct Answer is the default concise view.
Relevant History includes only events material to the question.
Evidence and Law exposes provenance already approved for publication.
Full Context cannot expose restricted evidence or internal reasoning.
A request outside the approved investigation scope becomes a scope-change request rather than a silent expansion.
Material limitations remain visible in every view.
A broader view must not imply greater certainty.
View ordering must not imply correctness or importance beyond the approved answer structure.

scope_change_boundary.in_scope_view: render approved content at different depth
scope_change_boundary.out_of_scope: new property, new target date, new legal issue, new requested outcome, new evidence question or materially broader investigation

hard_stops: Never alter property or date scope through a view switch.
Never expose restricted evidence through Full Context.
Never omit material limitations from a shorter view.
Never create a new legal conclusion while rendering a view.
Never treat a broader view as more authoritative than the approved answer.
